correctness.rationale: CRT yields unique (u,v,t) with -1<=t and u<b,v<a. Each two-coin pair contributes precisely 1+min(U,V) refinements. For t>=2 the j=1 term contributes >=a+1 plus two endpoints >=1, so no low-multiplicity arguments occur there. The t=0 rectangular min-levels give a+b-2k+1 cases; the t=1 triangular diagonal gives k-1, then a at the next level. Explicit linear optimization on both layers proves g_k for 1<=k<=a+1 and Sylvester genus proves the k=0 base. Dynamic programming independently agreed for 575 coprime pairs and 952360 n-values. All hypotheses and boundary cases were checked.

originality.rationale: Inspected the complete main-result sections of arXiv:2610.20899v2, whose general denumerant bounds and existence statement do not imply explicit first-phase counts or a uniform exact earliest slope transition. Arithmetic-progression p-numerical semigroup formulas require b=2a for ascending (a,b,a+b), excluded by the coprimality hypothesis a>=2. Recurrence-constrained Komatsu triples do not cover arbitrary coprime pairs. Searches for denumerant aliases, generalized Frobenius levels, semigroup genera, and co-generated denominations returned no covering statement; novelty remains a best-knowledge assessment with explicit risks.

value.rationale: The redundant third denomination is a natural minimal perturbation of two-generator representation counts: it preserves all representable integers while changing the entire multiplicity spectrum. The theorem determines the exact number of integers at each low representation multiplicity, the p-genus, and p-Frobenius uniformly for every coprime pair, including the sharp first non-linear transition at p=a+1. The endpoint is structurally forced by the emergence of a new CRT layer, not an arbitrary numerical window. This is a meaningful exact arithmetic boundary invariant and not a mere finite calculation or restatement of Sylvester genus.
